messages:
Alex: Heads-up — I'm onboarding horton-14b to staging. Weights are in s3://redwood-models/horton/14b/v1/ (sharded). Tokenizer uses BOS=1 (not 0). Anyone seen runtime hiccups from a nonzero BOS?
Maria: Noted. If BOS != 0 we need loader config normalization: set `tokenizer.bos_id: 1` and verify `pad_id`. I can add a fallback mapping in the loader to remap to internal convention.
Ryan: Ran a smoke load test and tritonserver segfaulted during dynamic batching warmup. Snippet from triton log:
```
E0620 12:11:02.345678 1 server.cc:123] TRITONSERVER_error: segmentation fault at 0x7f8b2
#0 0x7f8b2 in triton::backend::...
```
No useful stack that points to our model code.
Kevin: Segfault like that often points to CUDA/cuBLAS ABI mismatch. Which CUDA runtime was used to build the container? Driver mismatch between host and container will do this.
Maria: Staging nodes currently have NVIDIA driver 535.xx with CUDA 12.2 toolkit on the base image. Horton container image was built locally against CUDA 12.1 (I think). That could be it.
Lisa: To add — some newer triton builds also require different libstdc++/glibc symbols; we should ensure the base distro matches (we usually use ubuntu:22.04).
Alex: Good — so plan is rebuild container with CUDA 12.2 toolchain. Any suggestions for Triton version?
Kevin: For horton-14b we want Triton >= 24.02 for improved dynamic batch handling for sharded weights, but be careful: some flash-attention kernels got upstream changes.
Maria: Agree. I propose: CUDA 12.2, Triton 24.02, and rebuild with our standard `redwood-inference-runtime:ubuntu22-cuda12.2-triton24.02` tag. I'll open a CI job.
Ryan: Also saw tokenizer edge-case where `bos_id=1` leads to length off-by-one in kv-cache index mapping for some legacy loaders. Quick patch: when loading, if tokenizer.bos_id != model_config.bos_default then shift cache indices by -1 for first token. It's hacky but stops immediate failures.
Lisa: Let's avoid ad-hoc index hacks if possible. If loader mapping is correct (Maria's change) we shouldn't need cache shifts. But add unit test for kv-cache boundary to be safe.
Kevin: I'll kick off the rebuild: `./ci/build-image --cuda 12.2 --triton 24.02 --base ubuntu:22.04 --tag horton-14b-test` and then `./ci/push-if-green horton-14b-test`.
deploybot: Build queued — job id: 54211.
infra-bot: Staging node pool has driver 535.113, CUDA 12.2 runtime available. No reboot required.
Ryan: After rebuild I recommend a quick regression run: 50 eval prompts, check logits for top-5 token stability and run a 1k-token streaming test to ensure KV cache persistence. I can script that.
Alex: Can someone pick up code review for the loader config PR? It touches tokenizer mapping + new unit test. @Maria please ping when ready.
Maria: Will open PR in ~15m and add test vectors. Tagging reviewers: @Ryan, @Lisa.
Kevin: Once image build completes I'll run the triton smoke job in staging and report back. If segfault persists we'll capture `cuda-gdb` trace.
Lisa: Also add ENV `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=flash_attn` to the test run to validate fused kernel path; if it fails fall back to `aten` and note perf delta.
Alex: Awesome. Checklist for rollout: 1) loader config PR merged, 2) image rebuilt (12.2/24.02), 3) smoke + regen tests pass, 4) canary deploy to 1 node, 5) monitor latency/cost. Who owns canary?
Kevin: I can own canary deploy + rollback playbook.
Alex: Perfect. Thanks all — keep updates here and paste build job links.
Maria: PR opened: github.com/redwood/horton/PR/324 — adding test vectors and tokenizer.bos_id handling.
Kevin: Build succeeded: https://ci.redwood/jobs/54211 — image pushed. Kicking staging smoke now.
Ryan: Smoke run passed KV tests but saw slight token alignment diff for one prompt (likely tokenizer borderline). I'll open a small eval report.
Alex: Ok — leave canary until we resolve that eval diff. If it's a tokenizer mapping issue, we should be able to patch quickly.
Maria: Taking the eval diff now. Will report within an hour.
